title: GitHub Trending Summary - Daily - 2026-11-20
ranking_basis: Daily GitHub Trending ordering, with stars gained today captured as the momentum signal.
ranking_explanation: Uses the first ten non-fork repositories in the official GitHub daily Trending page order, rather than re-sorting the list; per-repository daily star gains are included as the page's momentum signal.
global_caveat: Snapshot captured at 2026-11-20 17:31 UTC. Star counts and Trending placement can change during the day and measure attention, not quality, security, or sustained adoption. GitHub Search API corroboration was rate-limited; repository metadata and default-branch HEADs were checked separately.

comparison_basis.description: Prior-day GitHub Trending ranks as reported in the November 20 comparison, referring to the November 19 snapshot.

themes.title: Agent workflows and skill ecosystems
themes.content: Claude-BugHunter and superpowers package reusable procedures; Cursor plugins standardizes extensions, while diagram-design and last30days-skill apply agent capabilities to visual work and research.

themes.title: Agent-ready interfaces and external context

themes.title: Model training and deployment

sections.title: Snapshot
sections.content: Snapshot time (UTC): 2026-11-20 17:31 UTC. Scope: Daily. Date range: 2026-11-20 through 2026-11-20. Ranking basis: daily GitHub Trending ordering, with displayed star gains as momentum context.

sections.title: Headline
sections.content: Agent-oriented development dominates today's front page: security and coding skill frameworks, agent-ready software interfaces, and plugin ecosystems lead the list. The signal is not only new AI tooling—established infrastructure and inference projects also appear among today's fastest-moving repositories.

sections.title: elementalsouls/Claude-BugHunter
sections.description: A Claude Code skill bundle for authorized bug hunting and red-team work, with vulnerability-class playbooks and reporting workflow.
sections.why_notable: It leads today's Trending list, and its README describes an unusually broad, structured security workflow rather than a single-purpose scanner.
sections.unique_caveat: Security testing capabilities should only be used against authorized targets and within the stated scope.

sections.title: obra/superpowers
sections.description: A composable skills framework that makes coding agents follow a deliberate software-development methodology.
sections.why_notable: Its strong daily momentum puts a process-oriented agent framework near the top; the README emphasizes design, planning, test-driven implementation, and review.

sections.title: HKUDS/CLI-Anything
sections.description: A toolkit and registry for giving agents structured command-line control of existing software.
sections.why_notable: It represents a practical alternative to brittle GUI automation, with stateful CLI workflows and structured output for agents.

sections.title: jingyaogong/minimind
sections.description: An educational, end-to-end project for training small language models from scratch.
sections.why_notable: Its full training pipeline—from pretraining and fine-tuning through preference optimization and tool use—stands out amid the agent tooling wave.

sections.title: cursor/plugins
sections.description: Cursor's official marketplace repository for plugins and integrations.
sections.why_notable: It shows the move toward a standardized, installable extension ecosystem for agent skills, rules, tools, and service integrations.

sections.title: firecrawl/firecrawl
sections.description: Web search, scraping, crawling, and structured extraction infrastructure aimed at agent workflows.
sections.why_notable: Its high daily gain highlights continued demand for turning live web content into machine-usable context.

sections.title: nginx/nginx
sections.description: The official NGINX Open Source repository.
sections.why_notable: A mature core-infrastructure project is a useful counterpoint to today's concentration of agent-focused tools.

sections.title: openvinotoolkit/openvino
sections.description: An open-source toolkit for optimizing and deploying AI inference.
sections.why_notable: Its appearance connects the agent trend to the practical runtime and deployment layer for AI models.

sections.title: cathrynlavery/diagram-design
sections.description: A design-focused diagram skill for coding agents, with self-contained HTML and SVG outputs.
sections.why_notable: It extends agent tooling beyond code generation into visual communication, with a large set of diagram patterns.

sections.title: mvanhorn/last30days-skill
sections.description: A research skill that gathers signals across social platforms and the wider web into a grounded brief.
sections.why_notable: It reflects demand for agent workflows that synthesize recent, cross-platform information rather than only edit code.

sections.title: Trending Technologies and Themes
sections.content: Agent workflows and skill ecosystems recur across Claude-BugHunter, superpowers, Cursor plugins, diagram-design, and last30days-skill. CLI-Anything and Firecrawl provide agent-ready software interfaces and web context. MiniMind and OpenVINO represent model training and deployment. In this ten-repository sample, Python is most common, TypeScript is next, and Shell, C, C++, and HTML are also represented.

sections.title: Notable Shifts
sections.content: Compared with the prior day's Trending snapshot, superpowers jumped from #14 to #2 (+12 places) and OpenVINO rose from #13 to #8 (+5). Cursor/plugins moved from #1 to #5, while last30days-skill fell from #3 to #10. Comparison basis: November 19 ranks reported at https://www.trendsmcp.ai/trending/github-trending-november-20-2026.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.content: The strongest signal is a shift from agents as standalone chat interfaces toward agents equipped with repeatable workflows, software controls, integrations, and fresh external context. At the same time, MiniMind and OpenVINO show continued interest in the model-building and inference stack beneath those applications. Trending placement and star gains indicate attention, not software quality, security, or long-term adoption.

sections.title: Sources and Method
sections.content: Primary source: https://github.com/trending?since=daily, observed 2026-11-20 17:31 UTC. Repository metadata was checked using GitHub REST API; current HEAD SHAs were verified by git ls-remote. The unauthenticated GitHub Search API was rate-limited, so no Search API result is claimed. Daily star gains are copied from the matching Trending page. README and first-party docs were consulted for leading agent, CLI, model-training, and plugin examples; no DeepWiki enrichment was used.
